advice: Propose one experiment: in the general SME multiply path, replace per-k index expressions with advancing row pointers. At the start of each output tile, set `ap0 = at + i`, `ap1 = at + i + second_row`, `bp0 = b + j`, and `bp1 = b + j + second_col`. Each reduction step loads from those pointers, then advances them by `n` only when another k step remains. Keep the existing predicates and ZA selectors, and retain the current tile and tail handling. This isolates address-generation overhead while keeping the FP32 operations and reduction order unchanged.
risks: The compiler may already form equivalent pointer increments, so the change may have no effect. Conditional final-step increments add a branch; unconditional increments risk forming pointers beyond the valid allocation at the final step. Verify no out-of-bounds pointer formation for odd dimensions and partial tiles, including n=1 and n<=0; check general correctness against the fixed 0.002 limit and then measure serially against fresh AC controls. Treat any score as unverified until those measurements; do not infer causality from noisy or joint results.
